> **Narrowed 2026-10-14 (Sue).** An open issue describes exactly the remaining work (backlog-workflow rule).
>
> **Resolved so far:** item 1 landed in 3069ef80 (pinned by tests/test_kinship_other_relative.py); the two tuples the original body contrasts no longer exist.
>
> **Remaining (this issue):** the partial-null policy (item 2), which is 24x larger than the body states: ~13 class-C/D keys -> [G, D, null] (Guyana triple -> [null, null, null]), tests extended, and a 'degeneracies that are the instrument' note in Peru/_/CONTENTS.org and Guatemala/_/CONTENTS.org.
>
> **Decision for @ligon:** Extend the header's conflation rule to the Affinity slot alone -- [G, D, null] for every 'X of head or spouse' and 'X or X-in-law' label (36,632 people, Affinity only): yes/no?

---
*Original text, kept for the evidence:*

kinship: `Otro Pariente` is undetermined by the instrument — the corpus files it three different ways

Split out of #684 / PR #691, where it was found and where the immediate fix landed.

## The finding

`Peru/1994/Documentation/m-encues.pdf`, "Pregunta Nº 1: Parentesco o relación con el jefe", defines B01 code 7 verbatim:

> Otro pariente (código 7) comprende a los parientes consanguíneos y de matrimonio con el jefe: hermano, tío, primo, consuegro, bisnieto, abuelo, cuñado, bisabuelo, sobrino.

Brother, uncle, cousin, co-parent-in-law, great-grandchild, grandfather, brother-in-law, great-grandfather, nephew. That single survey code spans **Generation −3..+3, Distance 0..2, and both affinities**.

`kinship.yml` filed `"Otro Pariente": [0, 0, consanguineal]` — "same generation, lineal, blood", which is Kroeber's cell for *ego itself*. That is not merely uninformative; it is **refuted by a document this repository ships**.

Affected: **884 Peruvian** people (4.58% of the roster, 474 households) and **596 Guatemalan** (1.58% of 37,771).

## What PR #691 did

Changed it to `[null, null, null]` — an explicit unknown — with the quotation above in a comment. Verified: a null tuple needs **no framework change** (`_load_kinship_map` does `tuple(vals)`; `_expand_kinship._component` returns `x[i]` for any tuple; `pd.array(..., Int64Dtype())` turns `None` into `pd.NA`), and because the key still *matches*, **no "unknown relationship labels" warning fires** — which matters, since such a warning's own text invites the next reader to supply a fresh guess.

Measured before/after, cold:

| | Generation nulls | Distance nulls | Affinity nulls |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peru before | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Peru after | 884 | 884 | 884 |
| Guatemala before | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Guatemala after | 596 | 596 | 596 |

No other value in either country changed. Guatemala's `Distance` still spans {0, 1}.

## What is left for this issue

**1. The canonical file is self-inconsistent on this exact concept.** Three filings of the same semantics:

| key | tuple | line |
|---|---|---|
| `Other relative of head or spouse` | `[0, 0, consanguineal]` | kinship.yml:282 |
| `Other relative of head` | `[0, 2, consanguineal]` | kinship.yml:631 |
| `Otro Pariente` | `[null, null, null]` | (now) |

Pick one policy and apply it to all "other relative" labels across the corpus. My view is that the null is right wherever the instrument conflates, but that should be a deliberate corpus-wide decision, not three accidents.

**2. Decide the general rule.** `Padre/Suegro` (Peru, 279 people) and Guyana's `Father/Mother/T-In-Law/M-In-Law` conflate exactly two tuples that differ only in `Affinity`. Is a partial null (`[1, 0, null]`) the right filing? That is expressible today and strictly more informative than either guess. Nothing in the corpus uses a partial null yet.

**3. Note the degeneracy that is *not* a bug.** Peru's `Distance` is 0 for every non-null person because ENNIV's ten codes contain no sibling or cousin category at all. Across the 33 countries with a cached roster, Peru is one of only three whose `Distance` is constant (with GhanaSPS and Serbia-and-Montenegro). That is the instrument, not the mapping — worth recording so nobody "fixes" it.

## Why this is filed rather than done

Changing a shared canonical entry is a cross-country decision. The Peru PR changed the one entry its own source refutes and measured the blast radius; the corpus-wide policy needs an owner.

comments.body: Another instance from the #797 corpus sweep: **EthiopiaRHS 1989** serves its 66 raw `Other` rows as a definite `[0, 0, unrelated]`. The table's own header (`EthiopiaRHS/_/categorical_mapping.org`) calls that a judgment call, and all five sibling waves carry grandchild / in-law / other-relative at 1.2-4.8% against 0.4% unrelated -- so the bucket is mostly kin. Candidate for the null tuple, on the precedent set here. Not changed; a cross-country policy call. -- Sue

Policy decided for the 'other relative' class (with @ligon, 2026-09-07) and landed in `3069ef80`: a plain 'other relative' label is `[null, null, consanguineal]` (a blood relative, generation and distance unrecorded -- these 15 keys had been sitting on Head's cell, 54,251 people in 25 countries); a label naming the spouse's relatives too ('of head or spouse', EHCVM 'autres parents du CM ou du conjoint') is `[null, null, null]` like `Otro pariente` (45,993 people, 7 countries). Head and Cousin untouched; `Other relative of head` leaves the cousin cell. Pinned by `tests/test_kinship_other_relative.py`. Still open here: the partial-null question for `Padre/Suegro` / GhanaLSS `Parent` (GLSS5-7) -- same shape, `[1, 0, null]`. -- Sue

**Three corrections to this issue, measured on `github/development` at `3cf124ca3`** while adjudicating #813. Two of its premises have expired, and the decision it names is much smaller than the decision it actually implies.

## 1. The two tuples this issue contrasts no longer exist

It tabulates `Other relative of head or spouse` → `[0, 0, consanguineal]` and `Other relative of head` → `[0, 2, consanguineal]` as evidence that the file is self-inconsistent. **Neither tuple is in `kinship.yml` today.** The null policy this issue argued for has already been written into the file's header and applied consistently — to **74,339 + 44,930** people. So item 1 is substantially done; what is left is narrower than the body reads.

## 2. "Nothing in the corpus uses a partial null yet" is false

`Adopted/Foster/Stepchild: [-1, 0, null]` serves **2,081** people. The partial null is not a hypothetical to be introduced; it is an existing pattern, and the question is whether to extend it, not whether to invent it.

## 3. The decision is ~24× bigger than the class this issue names

This issue frames the residual around blood-∪-in-law conflations (`Padre/Suegro`, Guyana's `Father/Mother/T-In-Law/M-In-Law`). Measured, that class governs **1,318** people — and note **903 of them are Serbia-and-Montenegro's**, which the issue does not mention.

The far larger class is *determinate generation and distance, conflated affinity* — `Sister/Brother of head or spouse` and its kin:

| country | people |
|---|---|
| Uganda | 20,959 |
| Serbia and Montenegro | 11,094 |
| CotedIvoire | 3,161 |
| **total** | **35,314** |

A fully consistent partial-null policy therefore has a maximum blast radius of **37,170 people, in the `Affinity` slot only** — generation and distance do not move. That is the number to decide against, not 1,318.

No tuple was changed; this is measurement only. The itemised basis is in the #813 adjudication comment and in `slurm_logs/2026-09-18_kinship_813/ADJUDICATION.org`.

**Ruling (@ligon, 2026-10-18)**, from the framework-backlog decision sheet: Yes. "X of head or spouse" and "X or X-in-law" labels become `[G, D, null]`, Affinity only; the Guyana triple becomes `[null, null, null]`. This is the same null-component rule as 2026-09-07.

title: DECISION: kinship -- extend the conflation rule to the Affinity slot alone ([G, D, null]) for 'X of head or spouse' / 'X or X-in-law' labels
